evidence.note: Plan lines function as a running checklist, methodically enumerating and ticking off resource families (products, prices, subscriptions, refunds, webhook endpoints, restricted keys) one by one — a generally accurate done-vs-remaining picture across the CRUD surface.

Maintained a persistent list of identified bugs (card-lookup-by-last4, confirm:true support, idempotency error caching) across several steps before a consolidated rewrite, showing state tracking of outstanding work rather than forgetting.
Explicitly noted concurrent same-key serialization was not tested ('hard to test with curl, but the lock mechanism is in place') — aware of a gap but chose not to close it.

Webhook retry/backoff worker, subscription billing worker, and events/deliveries were only tested superficially or not at all, yet the final submission claims 'fully implemented and tested' — the coverage picture did not distinguish verified from implemented-only for the deep traps.

reasoning: The agent kept a running, mostly-accurate checklist of the 12 resource families and worked through them without forgetting any, and it tracked outstanding bugs across steps — matching the level-5 anchor ('keeps a running checklist of endpoints/subsystems and their status, generally knows what remains'). It falls short of level 8 because the deep trap subsystems (webhook retry worker, billing worker, events deliveries, concurrent idempotency) were left superficially covered yet declared 'fully tested,' so major areas were effectively dropped from verification without the agent noticing or reallocating attention to them.
